input.quote: ARTICLE IV TERM I Subject to termination pursuant to this Agreement, the Non Exclusive license granted by Licensor to Licensee shall be for an initial period of 36 months, commencing from the acceptance date, (the \"Initial Period\").
input.rationale: The Term article commits us to a 36-month Initial Period and no provision anywhere gives Licensee any right to terminate without cause: Licensor's termination rights are cause-based (breach under Article IV and Article II, insolvency under Article XIX, change of control under Article XX, wind-up under Article XX(b)), and there is no refund mechanic at all. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under T4C and fails the fallback (which requires at least a 60-90 day Customer exit). We therefore added the shortest preferred-level clause: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and express confirmation that Licensor has no convenience right during the term. Licensor's 7-year unilateral renewal option is a RENEWAL issue and is not flagged here.

proposal.summary: Add a Licensee termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirm Licensor has no convenience right during the term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Initial Period is 36 months with no exit right for us, so we have added a convenience termination on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirmed Licensor cannot terminate for convenience during the term. If 30 days is unworkable we can move to 60-90 days' notice.

ops.text: Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor, in which case Licensor shall refund pro rata any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any renewal term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
